title: Sample preparation protocol for cross-sectional microscopy of hair fibers
author: Tina Lasisi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbwcipaw

steps.title: Prepare Plastic Chips
steps.instruction: Create thin polycaprolactone plastic chips for embedding.

substeps.instruction: Cut polycaprolactone plastic into 2x2cm squares.
Heat a metal block on a hot plate at 60 °C for 5 minutes.
Place a plastic square on the hot plate with parchment paper underneath for 30 seconds.
Cover the heated plastic with a square of parchment paper (5x5cm) and place the heated metal block on top for 30 seconds to flatten.
Remove the plastic (with parchment on both sides) and flatten between two cold metal blocks for 5 minutes.
Peel off parchment and remove the thinned plastic chips.
Cut plastic to desired dimensions using scissors or scalpel (recommended 20x10mm for most hairs or 20x5mm for very short hairs).
Take 3-5 hairs per sample.
Cut samples down to 5cm if they exceed this length.

steps.title: Embed Hair Fibers
steps.instruction: Embed hair fibers into the prepared plastic chips using a hot plate at 60 °C.

substeps.instruction: Place one prepared plastic chip on parchment paper on the heated block until translucent (approximately 30 seconds).
Using tweezers on each side, stretch hair fibers taut and parallel over the plastic, pressing them in until completely submerged.
Heat a second prepared plastic chip until translucent.
Carefully overlay the second chip over the first chip containing the hairs.
Apply a metal block over the top to flatten the sample for 15 seconds.
Remove the embedded sample and place between two cool blocks for 2 minutes.
Peel off parchment paper and trim excess hairs and plastic into a rectangular chip.
Store the sample in a cool room at 4 °C for at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Cut Embedded Samples
steps.instruction: Section the embedded chips to expose the hair cross-sections.

substeps.instruction: Place the chip under a press (e.g., PanaVise 502 Precision PanaPress with cable cutting attachment) or use a sharp razor/blade.
Cut the sample in half to create mirroring sections, or trim the top to expose the cross section.
Work in small batches and work quickly to prevent the chips from heating up due to body temperature or environment.
Immediately store samples in a cold room or freezer until imaging.

steps.title: Image Hair Cross-Sections
steps.instruction: Perform microscopy on the embedded hair samples.

substeps.instruction: Mount the hairs vertically using a clamp or stand.
Image each hair individually using a microscope capable of magnifying to 10x.
Do not leave samples unattended under the microscope lights to prevent melting.
Store samples immediately in a cool room or freezer after imaging.
